intro.author: Not named. Jewish tradition in the Talmud says Samuel wrote the early chapters and the prophets Gad and Nathan completed the work (compare 1 Chronicles 29:29). Samuel dies in chapter 25, so others finished the account.
intro.written: Uncertain. A note that Ziklag 'pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day' (27:6) suggests a final form after the kingdom split around 930 BC; many scholars date it later still
intro.audience: Israel, learning how kingship began and why God chose David's family
intro.setting: The story opens near the end of the judges, with a corrupt priesthood at Shiloh and the Philistines pressing in with iron weapons. It covers roughly a century, from Samuel's birth to Saul's death, traditionally around 1010 BC. First and Second Samuel were one book in Hebrew; the Greek translation divided it.
intro.purpose: To show how Israel moved from judges to kings, and that God honors those who honor him: Eli's house falls, Saul is rejected, and David, 'a man after his own heart,' is chosen.
intro.bigIdea: God lifts up the humble, brings down the proud, and looks on the heart.
